title: The Kervaire theorem for groups
main_claim: For every group A and every word w in A*<t> whose t-exponent sum is ±1, the map A -> (A*<t>)/<<w>> is injective. The Kervaire conjecture follows as a corollary: (A*<t>)/<<w>> is nontrivial whenever A is nontrivial.
coverage:
I read every section in full (introduction, phase, degree, diagram, topology) and checked each step of the proof chain by hand.
(1) Phase-subadditivity lemma in M_b(group vN algebra): the derivative formula for z^r with traciality, the bound tau(f'(W)B) <= tau(B) when f' <= 1 and B >= 0, the smoothing f_eps (f_eps' <= 1, pointwise limit to h including the cut value h(1)=0), and the bounded-convergence passage. I also tested it numerically: 20k random unitaries of size up to 5, including eigenvalues near the cut; the maximum violation was about 7e-16, which is rounding error.
(2) Fixed-space lemma: the pair-cancelling homotopy diag(X,I)R_u diag(I,X^{-1})R_u^{-1} (endpoints verified); the dimension of the incidence manifold, m^2-k^2, so dim M = m^2; uniqueness of the preimage of I; the derivative dG0 = [[eps A, 2Z*], [-2Z, -B]], which covers every skew-Hermitian matrix exactly once, so I is a regular value; and the mod-2 degree argument.
(3) Planar theorem: equal numbers k of positive and negative disks; corner weights and JSJ = S^{-1} checked on both kinds of disk; SJ is a self-adjoint unitary with trace 0, so l(SJ) = nk/2; J restricted to V_- is diag(X^{-s_i}), and the lemma is applied with signs -s_i; Theta^2 = I follows from gamma_{theta d} = -gamma_d; J conjugates J Theta to its inverse, giving fixed-space dimension >= 2k and l(J Theta) <= nk-k; the cycle identity sum_j h(zeta^j lambda) = (d-1)/2 + h(lambda^d) and the circuit weight L(r_z^{-1}); Euler characteristic gives q = nk-2k+2; the boundary sum tends to 3nk/2 - k + tau(h(L(r0^{-1}))); the one-sided limits (trivial circles tend to 1, the exceptional circle is right-continuous at the cut); and faithfulness.
(4) Topology: the realization map f on the punctured disk; the piecewise-affine approximation u' within 1/12, with the level z in (1/3, 2/3), so u stays more than 1/4 from the wedge point on the level and v is constant on the bands; one arc endpoint per t-interval, with opposite signs at the two ends; the corner labels are preserved; and the innermost-component induction (minimality of D(C) excludes nested components, inner disks carry v, so their words are trivial; Theorem 4.1 then makes the outer word trivial, and D(C) is filled in).
